reason: The text contains several named characters who are not leaders. Most notably, Jotham (יוֹתָם), the youngest son of Jerubbaal, is explicitly named and plays a significant role in the narrative—he escapes the massacre of his brothers and pronounces a prophetic curse from Mount Gerizim—but he is not a leader. He is a fugitive survivor who delivers a parable warning. Additionally, Gaal son of Ebed (גַּעַל בֶּן־ עָבֶד) is a named character who, while gaining the trust of the people of Shechem, is not presented as an official leader or ruler. While Abimelech, Zebul (the governor), and Jerubbaal are named leaders, the presence of Jotham as a non-leader named character invalidates the statement.
